input:
Basis

This design report sets out the design of a distillation column, and the basis on which the design rests is described in this opening section. The design throughput of the column is 60 t per day, and the separation duty that the column is required to achieve is the removal of 92% of the key component from the feed stream. The materials basis for the design is 316L stainless steel for all wetted parts, and this is stated here at the outset so that the materials discussion later in the report can build upon it. The feed to the column is received from the upstream equipment in the state in which that equipment delivers it, and the design treats the stated separation duty as the governing requirement against which the column is sized, in the sense that the sizing work described below is directed towards meeting that duty at the stated throughput while at the same time providing a column that can be fabricated, installed, and operated within the wider unit of which the column forms a part.

Sizing

The sizing of the column is concerned in large part with the diameter and the height of the vessel, and each of these dimensions is governed by a different set of considerations. The diameter is governed principally by the vapour traffic that the column is required to handle, since the rising vapour must be accommodated without excessive entrainment of liquid and without the column approaching a flooded condition at the design throughput. The height, by contrast, is governed by the number of separation stages that the duty demands and by the spacing that is provided between the internals that deliver those stages, together with the additional allowances that are made at the top and the bottom of the vessel for disengagement and for the liquid inventory that is held in the base. The selection of the internals themselves, whether trays or packing, is made with reference to the separation duty, the properties of the fluids being handled, and the pressure drop that can be accepted across the column, and the sizing is carried out on a consistent basis so that the diameter, the height, and the internals together deliver the stated removal of the key component. It is also the case that the traffic within the column is established by the reflux that is returned at the top and by the vapour that is raised at the base, so that the diameter is in effect sized for that internal traffic rather than for the feed rate in isolation, and the stage efficiency has a bearing on the height through the number of actual stages that the internals are required to provide.

Materials

The materials of construction are an important aspect of the design, and the grade that is specified in the basis section is adopted for all of the wetted parts of the column, including the shell, the internals, and the nozzles through which the process fluids enter and leave the vessel. The selection of a stainless grade for the wetted envelope reflects the corrosive character of the service and the need for the column to retain its integrity over the design life without the wall thickness being consumed by corrosion at an unacceptable rate. Attention is also given in the design to the joints between the parts, to the gaskets and bolting that those joints require, and to the compatibility of each of these items with the fluids and the temperatures that they will encounter, as well as to the practical questions of welding, fabrication, and inspection access, all of which have a bearing on whether the specified materials can be realised in the finished equipment.

Risks

Two items are identified in this report as open risks, namely fouling and turndown, and it should be clearly understood that neither of these items is resolved within the scope of the present report. Fouling is a concern because deposits that accumulate on the internal surfaces of the column can progressively reduce the effective capacity of the internals and increase the pressure drop across the column, and the rate at which such deposits might accumulate cannot be established with confidence from the information that is currently available, since the fouling history of the feed in comparable service is not sufficiently documented. Turndown is a concern because the column will be required to operate below its design throughput for parts of its working life, and the behaviour of the internals at reduced rates, in particular the risks of weeping, maldistribution, and a loss of separation efficiency, has not yet been examined across the full operating range that the unit may demand. Both items are therefore carried forward as open items, to be addressed through further work and through the operating data that will become available in due course, and they are recorded here so that they are not lost sight of as the design is developed further. Until such time as these two items can be closed out, the design must be regarded as conditional in respect of both its capacity and its operating range.
target:
Basis

The design throughput of the column is 60 t per day, and the separation duty is the removal of 92% of the key component from the feed. Wetted parts are 316L stainless steel. The feed is received from the upstream equipment in the state that equipment delivers it, and the design treats the stated separation duty as the governing requirement: the column is sized to meet that duty at the stated throughput, as part of the wider unit, and the sizing, materials and risks sections that follow all rest on the basis stated here. The duty is a removal duty on the key component, and the performance of the column is judged against that removal at the design throughput, not against a product purity that the basis does not state. The basis is stated at the design throughput, and the feed rate and the duty are the pair of figures against which every later section is checked: a change to either reopens the sizing, and a change to the specified grade reopens the materials section.

Sizing

Diameter and height are governed by different considerations. The diameter is governed by the vapour traffic the column must handle: the rising vapour is accommodated without excessive entrainment of liquid and without the column approaching a flooded condition at the design throughput, with margin held between the operating point and the flooding limit. The height is governed by the number of separation stages the duty demands and by the spacing between the internals that deliver those stages, with allowances at the top of the vessel for disengagement of liquid from the leaving vapour and at the base for the liquid inventory held there. The internals, trays or packing, are selected against the separation duty, the properties of the fluids handled, and the pressure drop that can be accepted across the column. Diameter, height and internals are sized on one consistent basis, so that the three together deliver the stated removal of the key component at the design throughput, and no dimension is carried from a standard size where the duty requires otherwise. The traffic inside the column is set by the reflux returned at the top and the vapour raised at the base, and the diameter sized for the design throughput is sized for that traffic and not for the feed rate alone. Stage efficiency enters the height through the number of actual stages the internals must provide for the separation the duty demands, and the spacing allowed between stages carries the maintenance and inspection access the internals require over the life of the column.

Materials

The grade specified in the basis is adopted for all wetted parts: the shell, the internals, and the nozzles through which the process fluids enter and leave. A stainless grade is specified for the wetted envelope because the service is corrosive and the column must retain its integrity over the design life without the wall being consumed by corrosion at a rate the design cannot absorb. The joints between parts are designed with the main envelope: the gaskets and bolting those joints require are selected for compatibility with the fluids and temperatures they will meet, and the welds, the fabrication sequence and the access for inspection are settled with the material selection rather than after it, since a grade that cannot be welded, formed or inspected in the finished geometry is not a usable specification however well it resists the service. The same discipline applies to the smaller wetted items: instrument connections and drain and vent nozzles take the specified grade as well, since a single weaker item in the wetted envelope sets the corrosion performance of the whole vessel. Non-wetted parts stand outside that requirement and follow the general standard for the unit.

Risks

Fouling and turndown are open items. Neither is resolved in this report. Fouling is a risk because deposits accumulating on the internal surfaces reduce the effective capacity of the internals and raise the pressure drop across the column over time, and the rate at which deposits would accumulate cannot be established from the information currently available: the fouling history of the feed in comparable service is not documented well enough to support a rate, and no allowance in the sizing rests on one. Turndown is a risk because the column will operate below its design throughput for parts of its working life, and the behaviour of the internals at reduced rates has not been examined across the operating range the unit may demand: weeping, maldistribution and loss of separation efficiency are the failure modes at low rates, and each would show first as a shortfall against the stated removal duty. Both items are carried forward as open items, for further work and for the operating data that will settle them, and they are recorded here so that the limits of the design as it stands are stated in the report itself. Until the two items are closed, the design is issued with its capacity and its operating range both conditional: the capacity conditional on the fouling behaviour of the actual feed, and the range conditional on the behaviour of the internals at reduced rates.
